title: Graded Relevance: Visual Guide
outline: 1. Binary Loses Levels | a four-result ranking with per-rank grade steppers and a squashing threshold, showing AP computed from the collapsed binary vector beside nDCG computed from the grades | binary AP is identical whether the grade-3 answer sits at rank 1 or rank 3, and the threshold you squash at can itself decide the winner

2. Gain, Then Discount | reorderable grades [3, 0, 2, 1] with a linear-versus-exponential gain toggle, per-rank contribution bars and CG beside DCG | cumulative gain is order-blind at 6 whatever the order, the log2(i+1) discount is what makes position count, and the gain transform is a documented utility assumption

3. Divide By Ideal | six grade steppers plus a cutoff slider, with the observed list shown against the ideal sorted list and DCG, IDCG and nDCG@k | normalization by the ideal ordering puts every query on one scale, the cutoff is part of the metric because IDCG truncates with it, and zero IDCG is undefined and needs a declared policy

4. MAP Or nDCG | two systems holding the same two relevant documents in different orders, with steppers for what each document is worth and a relevance-model toggle | MAP always prefers the uninterrupted set while nDCG follows the grades, so the winner flips when the best document is buried, and the choice follows the product's relevance model rather than familiarity
